operations.evidence: The publication is labelled accredited official statistics.
Accreditation supports publication quality but does not make national justice statistics parcel-level evidence.
The bulletin applies to England and Wales and covers January to December 2025.
National annual scope cannot be attributed to an exact parcel.
1.59 million individuals were formally dealt with by the criminal justice system in the latest year.
An individual can be counted more than once and the total is not a local risk rate.
The number formally dealt with increased by 3% and was the highest since 2017.
A national change does not identify parcel-level public safety.
Around 226,300 out-of-court resolutions were issued in 2025.
Out-of-court resolution volumes are not parcel-level incident evidence.
Out-of-court resolutions increased by 7% from about 212,100 to 226,300.
The annual change cannot be used as an exact-address safety score.
181,700 community resolutions were issued in 2025.
The count reflects police disposal activity rather than local prevalence.
Community resolutions increased by 11% from 163,700 to 181,700.
Changes can reflect policing practice and cannot be assigned to a parcel.
Prosecutions increased by 3% in the latest year.
National prosecution changes do not measure exact-place exposure.
Convictions increased by 1% in the latest year.
Convictions may relate to offences from earlier periods and are not parcel evidence.
